mechanism: Three separately-trained components: V (a VAE) compresses each frame to a 32-D latent z; M (an MDN-RNN) models p(z_{t+1} | a_t, z_t, h_t), a probability distribution over next latents conditioned on action; C (a tiny linear controller, ~867 params) maps [z_t, h_t] to actions and is trained by CMA-ES evolution. Most parameters live in V+M (the world model), so C has a tiny credit-assignment problem in compressed latent space. Because M models a distribution, the agent can roll the dream forward without real interaction — and a temperature τ controls dream uncertainty during policy training.
invariant: Compress observations → predict future of the compressed representation → train a small policy in the compressed-prediction space. Separating the world model from the policy lets each be small individually because they're decoupled; lumping them together loses the leverage.
prediction: An agent trained entirely inside the hallucinated dream generated by V+M still solves the real-environment task when transferred back. Demonstrated on CarRacing-v0 (906±21 vs ~838 prior SOTA, first to solve) and VizDoom Take Cover (>750 step survival).
failure_mode: The policy can exploit imperfections in M during dream training — find adversarial states where M's predictions are wrong but exploitable for reward — and then fail in reality. Temperature τ partially mitigates by adding uncertainty to dreams but does not solve it. The deeper failure: when the environment shifts, V/M become stale and imagined dynamics drift from reality.
first_principle: Most learning shouldn't happen in reality — reality is the slowest, most expensive, least controllable training environment available; once you have a tolerable predictive model of it, the rest of optimization belongs in imagination. Mental rehearsal, scenario planning, simulation, and self-play all rest on the same principle.
anti_pattern: Treating model-based RL as Dyna-style 'use the model to simulate one or two steps ahead inside an otherwise model-free pipeline' — still spends most wall-clock in real interactions. Ha & Schmidhuber's claim is stronger: the policy should LIVE INSIDE the world model. Conflating M's job (predict z_{t+1}) with C's job (choose a_t) loses the decoupling that makes each component small.
transferability_test: LLM tool-using agents building internal scratchpad models and imagining tool calls before executing. Recommender systems modeling user preference dynamics and optimizing in imagination before A/B. Construction-site planners imagining multi-step interventions. Athletes/surgeons mentally rehearsing in compressed mental models. Tabletop strategy exercises.
one_sentence_compression: Compress observations to a small latent code, learn to predict the next code, and train your policy entirely in imagination — reality is just data for the compressor and predictor, not the place where the policy is searched.
